name: The Alchemist's Road
description: Santiago's journey from The Alchemist by Paulo Coelho through real places at real scale, about 4370 km: Andalusia, Tangier, across the Sahara to Al-Fayoum and the Pyramids. The map is real terrain (Natural Earth).

andalusia.name: Andalusian Pastures
andalusia.text: A young shepherd sleeps among his sheep and dreams, twice, of a treasure by the Pyramids.

old-church.name: The Ruined Church
old-church.text: A roofless church with a sycamore growing where the sacristy once stood.

tarifa.name: Tarifa
tarifa.text: In the town square an old man who says he is a king asks for a tenth of your flock.

strait.name: Strait of Gibraltar
strait.text: You sell your sheep and cross the sea to Africa.

tangier.name: Tangier
tangier.text: Robbed on your first day, in a city where you don't speak the language.

crystal-shop.name: The Crystal Merchant
crystal-shop.text: A year of polishing glass, selling tea and saving money. The shop has never done better.

sahara-edge.name: Edge of the Sahara
sahara-edge.text: A caravan of camels leaves the last well behind. An Englishman reads books about alchemy.

deep-sahara.name: Heart of the Sahara
deep-sahara.text: Weeks of sand and silence. You learn to listen to the desert.

al-fayoum.name: Al-Fayoum Oasis
al-fayoum.text: Palms, wells and a woman named Fatima. Two hawks fight in the sky, and you read an omen.

alchemist-tent.name: The Alchemist's Tent
alchemist-tent.text: A man in black on a white horse agrees to take you across the desert.

wind-rock.name: The Rock of the Wind
wind-rock.text: Held at a desert camp, you have three days to turn yourself into the wind.

giza.name: Pyramids of Giza
giza.text: You dig by the Pyramids, and a stranger's words tell you the treasure lies back home, under the sycamore.

story.reading: You like the sheep, but you also like books and new horizons.
story.omens: Two stones, one black and one white, help you when you can't decide.
story.war: Tribes are at war in the desert, and the caravan moves only at night.
story.lead: The alchemist shows you a trick with lead. It's not the gold that matters.

facts.first-print: The Alchemist first came out in Brazil in 1988. The first publisher printed about 900 copies and chose not to reprint it.
facts.camino: Two years earlier, in 1986, Coelho walked the Camino de Santiago, the pilgrims' road across northern Spain.
facts.tarifa-point: Tarifa's headland is the southernmost point of continental Europe.
facts.strait-width: At its narrowest the Strait of Gibraltar is only about 14 km wide; on clear days Africa is visible from Spain.
facts.ibn-battuta: Ibn Battuta, one of the greatest travellers of the Middle Ages, was born in Tangier in 1304.
facts.alchemy-word: The word alchemy came into European languages from Arabic al-kīmiyā, and chemistry grew out of it.
facts.sahara-size: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, about 9 million km², roughly the size of the United States.
facts.not-all-sand: Most of the Sahara is not dunes at all but rocky plateaus and gravel plains.
facts.camel-drink: A thirsty camel can drink more than 100 litres of water in a few minutes.
facts.fayoum: Al-Fayoum is a real oasis in a desert depression west of the Nile, fed by an ancient canal and home to Lake Qarun.
facts.emerald-tablet: The Emerald Tablet, a short cryptic text attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, was a foundation of European alchemy.
facts.great-pyramid: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest structure built by people for about 3,800 years.
facts.translations: The Alchemist holds a Guinness World Record as the most translated book by a living author.

desert-day.name: Caravan Pace
desert-day.description: Walk 20 km in a single day.

wind.name: Become the Wind
wind.description: Reach the Rock of the Wind.

treasure.name: Where the Treasure Is
treasure.description: Reach the Pyramids and learn where the treasure is.
